_comment: The Phase 0 lab tests of the playbook (T1 to T23) and the tests OpenMove adds (M1 to M4), as guided procedures. scope 'retype' = needed before the retype path (class A and B, OpenStack APIs only) may change a cloud; 'staged' = needed only for the staged method (class C), which is not built. The wording is a summary; the playbook is the authority.

tests.title: Standard retype of a snapshot-free attached volume
tests.proves: The plain path works on this build: compute connectivity, Nova copy, completion, the target driver.
tests.pass: The volume is on the target back-end with the same id; the instance never paused and its I/O continued; the source is cleaned up.
tests.how: Pick a test instance with an attached volume of the source type. Dry run, run, sign G2 and G3, release, then read the instance console and the volume state after the post-check.

tests.title: Full staged move of a detached volume with three snapshots
tests.proves: History rebuild, record creation and direct completion.
tests.pass: Three snapshots exist after completion and a volume created from the oldest has the expected content.
tests.how: Staged method (class C): not built.

tests.title: Full staged move of an attached volume with three snapshots under a write load
tests.proves: The live cutover with a pre-seeded destination.
tests.pass: No guest I/O errors, no pause, checksums of a file written during the copy are correct, snapshots usable, attachment intact after a hard reboot.
tests.how: Staged method (class C): not built.

tests.title: The same as T3 on a boot-from-volume instance
tests.proves: Root volumes swap correctly on this Nova build.
tests.pass: The instance reboots from the target volume.
tests.how: Staged method (class C): not built. For the retype path see M1.

tests.title: Which attachment flow this release negotiates
tests.proves: Whether the old or the new attachment flow is used, so later tests use the same one.
tests.pass: The flow is recorded from the cinder-volume log.
tests.how: Move one attached test volume and read the cinder-volume log on the Cinder host.

tests.title: Rollback R2 after G3
tests.proves: The pre-cutover rollback leaves nothing behind.
tests.pass: Source unchanged, migration status cleared, no destination record, no staging volume, instance unlocked.
tests.how: Staged method (class C): not built.

tests.title: Interrupted cutover
tests.proves: What happens if the block copy is aborted.
tests.pass: Nova reports the swap failed; Cinder resets the source to in-use; leftovers are cleaned up; the instance keeps running on the source.
tests.how: Staged method (class C): not built. For the retype path see M3.

tests.title: Rollback R3 after G4
tests.proves: A migrated volume can be moved back.
tests.pass: The volume is back on the source back-end with the same id; as the tenant, snapshot, extend, attach, detach and create-from-snapshot all work; the cloud's view of it is unchanged. Leftovers on the array are listed.
tests.how: Use Reverse on one moved volume inside the soak, then try the tenant actions.

tests.title: Snapshot churn during staging
tests.proves: Reconciliation catches a snapshot created and one deleted.
tests.pass: The final chain on the array matches Cinder.
tests.how: Staged method (class C): not built.

tests.title: Tenant actions during the freeze
tests.proves: What a tenant can still do to a volume that is migrating.
tests.pass: Snapshot create, volume delete and extend are refused; detach is blocked by the instance lock; a snapshot delete is handled.
tests.how: Staged method (class C): not built. For the retype path, try the same actions on a volume while it is retyping and record what Cinder says.

tests.title: Throughput measurement
tests.proves: Time per GiB on this hardware, for batch planning.
tests.pass: The figures are written down.
tests.how: Time a move of a known size from the run's events (retype sent to post-check).

tests.title: Standard retype of a detached volume
tests.proves: The cinder-volume host of the source can copy through to the target.
tests.pass: The volume is on the target, same id, equal checksum, source cleaned up.
tests.how: Move one detached test volume with a known checksum and compare it after.

tests.title: Instance operations after a swap
tests.proves: Nova's swap leaves a usable domain and a correct block device mapping.
tests.pass: Soft and hard reboot, guest shutdown then start, and live migration to a second compute host all succeed.
tests.how: After T1, run the four operations on the instance.

tests.title: Restart nova-compute, then libvirtd, in the middle of a copy
tests.proves: What an orphaned job looks like and whether it recovers.
tests.pass: The guest ends on one consistent disk, the volume is in-use again, and there is no guest I/O error.
tests.how: Restart the services on the compute host while an attached move is running; then read what OpenMove and the cloud report.

tests.title: Field sync and row identity
tests.proves: A tenant edit made during the copy survives and no tenant-visible field changes.
tests.pass: Rename and metadata edit are present afterwards; only the expected database columns changed.
tests.how: Staged method (class C): not built. For the retype path the post-check compares the identity fields.

tests.title: Failed swap: recovery of the staging volume
tests.proves: The array returns the staged volume and its snapshots.
tests.pass: The staged volume and every snapshot are recovered and a second attempt succeeds.
tests.how: Staged method (class C): not built.

tests.title: Type, access and quota after the move, as a tenant
tests.proves: A tenant sees a normal volume.
tests.pass: As a non-admin: show, extend, snapshot, delete snapshot, create from snapshot and retype all work; per-type quota usage recorded before and after.
tests.how: Sign in as a tenant of a project whose volume was moved and try each action.

tests.title: The target driver against the real array
tests.proves: The driver and its library work with this array software release.
tests.pass: Create, snapshot, create from snapshot, extend, attach, detach and delete all pass on the target back-end; the delete behaviour (recoverable window) is recorded.
tests.how: Run the actions on a throw-away volume of the target type.

tests.title: Clone read speed and its effect on tenants
tests.proves: The clone QoS gives an acceptable rate without hurting other volumes.
tests.pass: MB/s at the chosen QoS; other volumes' latency stays inside the owner's limit.
tests.how: Staged method (class C): not built.

tests.title: Block copy onto a pre-seeded destination
tests.proves: The copy lands on a staging volume that already holds the newest snapshot image.
tests.pass: No difference between the target and the rollback clone.
tests.how: Staged method (class C): not built.

tests.title: A volume extended after a snapshot
tests.proves: A snapshot taken before an extend gives a smaller clone and the chain copy handles it.
tests.pass: Both array snapshots exist and the tail of the first image reads as zero.
tests.how: Staged method (class C): not built.

tests.title: The instance lock is read and respected
tests.proves: OpenMove sees the lock and never unlocks one it did not set.
tests.pass: With the compute API at microversion 2.9 or later the lock shows as true or false; a tenant's lock is left in place by a move; below 2.9 the move is refused.
tests.how: Lock a test instance as a tenant, move its volume, read the lock afterwards. Run in the lab (docs/LAB.md).

tests.title: A change between staging and the swap
tests.proves: A tenant who extends, transfers or retypes the volume, or snapshots it, before the freeze neither breaks the move nor fails the post-check.
tests.pass: (a) A volume extended during the copy: the staging volume grows to match, the new region is copied and compared at the final copy, and the move completes. (b) A volume extended after the cutover started but before the freeze: the move is rolled back with nothing frozen. (c) A volume transferred to another project before the freeze: the post-check passes against the capture taken at the end of the freeze. (d) A volume retyped between two source types: the move is given up before anything changes. (e) A snapshot made before the freeze is copied or stops the cutover; it never fails the post-check.
tests.how: Lab (docs/LAB.md) and, for the Purity form of the array extend, the customer's FlashArray. Do each case on a spare class C volume while the move waits in the recheck phase. Check the form `purevol setattr --size <GiB>G <volume>` on your Purity release once: OpenMove's own adapters do not call it yet.

tests.title: Retype of a boot-from-volume instance
tests.proves: A root volume moves by retype on this Nova build.
tests.pass: The instance reboots from the target back-end and its block device mapping points at it.
tests.how: Move the volume of a boot-from-volume test instance, then hard-reboot the instance. Run in the lab (docs/LAB.md).

tests.title: The way back by retype
tests.proves: Reverse restores the source back-end, the attachment and a running instance.
tests.pass: Back on the source type and back-end, attachment intact, instance ACTIVE and unlocked.
tests.how: Use Reverse on an attached test volume inside the soak. Run in the lab (docs/LAB.md).

tests.title: A service stops during a move
tests.proves: OpenMove sends nothing more, does not guess, and finishes correctly when the service returns.
tests.pass: While the Cinder API, then the Cinder volume service, are stopped for a minute during a move, no second change is sent and no unknown outcome is accepted; the move ends correctly afterwards. HALT pressed during a move stops all changes.
tests.how: Stop the service on the Cinder host during the retype, start it again, press HALT once. Run in the lab (docs/LAB.md).

tests.title: A volume with a snapshot is not retyped
tests.proves: The pre-flight keeps class C out, and a retype that Cinder accepts and silently undoes is detected.
tests.pass: The dry run refuses the volume; if a retype is sent by hand, the result is recorded and the engine rolls back rather than calling it a success.
tests.how: Try one volume with a snapshot. In the lab Cinder accepted the retype and undid it, and OpenMove detected it (docs/LAB.md).
